claims.text: High configurational entropy creates substantial local lattice distortions in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Local lattice distortions slow atomic diffusion at high temperatures.
Slower atomic diffusion inhibits phase segregation.
Slower atomic diffusion inhibits nanoparticle coarsening.
Phase segregation and coarsening compromise structural and chemical stability.
The proposed initial high-entropy nanoalloy is uniformly alloyed and has a near-equiatomic distribution of its constituent elements.
An inert annealing atmosphere minimizes oxidation.
High-temperature annealing activates significant atomic diffusion.
Lattice strain and distortion induced by high configurational entropy reduce diffusion kinetics.
Entropy-stabilized lattice distortions impede diffusion of constituent atoms.
Impeded constituent-atom diffusion delays or prevents phase separation during high-temperature exposure.
Impeded constituent-atom diffusion delays or prevents nanoparticle coarsening during high-temperature exposure.
High-entropy nanoalloys will retain more uniform phase distributions than analogous low-entropy controls under identical high-temperature conditions.
High-entropy nanoalloys will coarsen more slowly than analogous low-entropy controls under identical high-temperature conditions.
High-entropy nanoalloys will have slower diffusion than analogous low-entropy controls under identical high-temperature conditions.
Low-entropy or less-equiatomic controls are expected to undergo faster diffusion, greater phase segregation, and greater coarsening.
At relatively low temperatures, differences in diffusion kinetics and structural evolution between high-entropy and low-entropy nanoalloys may not be significant.
Direct experimental evidence connecting high configurational entropy to slowed nanoscale diffusion at high temperature is limited.
The hypothesis is falsified if the high-entropy samples do not have slower diffusion, or have similar or greater segregation or comparable coarsening relative to controls under identical conditions.
